summary.en: Classify characters with ctype.h and convert case while respecting argument and locale rules.
summary.bn: ctype.h দিয়ে ক্যারেক্টারের ধরন দেখো আর আর্গুমেন্ট ও লোকেলের নিয়ম মেনে অক্ষরের কেস বদলাও।

notes: The listed ctype.h operations are available in C89 and later. Their argument-domain restrictions still apply in C17 and C23. A newer compiler does not convert these byte routines into a general Unicode text library.

examples.title: Classify a mixed token
examples.explanationHtml: Three letters and three digits are counted. The exclamation mark belongs to neither category.

quiz.explanation: ctype.h provides byte character classification and case conversion.
True is any nonzero result, so equality with one is unreliable.

quiz.prompt: What happens to '7' under tolower in the initial C locale?
options: It becomes 7 as an integer digit
quiz.explanation: A non-uppercase character is returned unchanged.

quiz.prompt: Which argument is valid for ctype when a buffer uses plain char?
options: A possibly negative text[i] without conversion
quiz.explanation: Conversion keeps the argument in the unsigned-char range.

quiz.prompt: Why store getchar results in int before checking EOF?
options: int can distinguish byte values from EOF
quiz.explanation: Converting to char first can lose the end-of-input distinction.

quiz.prompt: Does isspace recognize a tab in the C locale?
quiz.explanation: The whitespace set includes tab and newline along with space.

quiz.prompt: Will per-byte toupper correctly uppercase all Bangla and Unicode text?
quiz.explanation: Byte-oriented locale functions are not a general Unicode text API.

quiz.prompt: How many letters and digits occur in CSE212!?
quiz.explanation: The punctuation is excluded from both counts.

quiz.prompt: What normalized results describe a tab, uppercase A and digit test on A?
quiz.explanation: Whitespace and uppercase tests succeed; the digit test fails.

quiz.prompt: What two forms of Lab-204 are printed by the case converters?
quiz.explanation: Case conversion changes letters alone in the C locale.

examQuestions.question: Explain the unsigned char cast in isalpha((unsigned char)text[i]) and why predicate results should be normalized.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A negative char other than EOF is outside the required argument domain and causes undefined behavior. Casting a stored byte to unsigned char gives a permitted value. Classification succeeds with any nonzero result, so use !=0 when adding Boolean counts or producing portable numeric output.

examQuestions.question: Read a line of 0 to 80 ASCII characters and newline. Print Line: then a normalized line with internal whitespace runs replaced by one space and no leading or trailing whitespace.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <ctype.h>

int main(void)
{
    char text[82];
    puts("Line:");
    if (fgets(text, sizeof text, stdin) == NULL) {
        return 1;
    }
    text[strcspn(text, "\n")] = '\0';
    char result[81];
    size_t used = 0;
    int pending = 0;
    for (size_t i = 0; text[i] != '\0'; i++) {
        if (isspace((unsigned char)text[i])) {
            pending = used != 0;
        } else {
            if (pending) {
                result[used++] = ' ';
            }
            result[used++] = text[i];
            pending = 0;
        }
    }
    result[used] = '\0';
    puts(result);
    return 0;
}
